apiContracts: GET-only; optional q parameter is trimmed and capped at 80 characters by rejecting longer input with HTTP 400 before SQL preparation; accepted input uses literal LIKE wildcard escaping; max 50 matching authors or 100 directory authors; aggregate output only.
dataEntities: No new entities. Aggregate data is derived only from novels that are published and have rights_status in original, public_domain, licensed or authorized.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Reuses existing novels and author display-name fields. No schema changes.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: Existing /author/:name profile URLs and GET /api/public-authors remain compatible; the endpoint is hardened without changing its response fields.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Revert the page, renderer, navigation and route additions together. The hardened read-only API can remain or be reverted independently; no data repair is required.

uiLifecycle.ssrBehavior: The Worker serves a dedicated authors.html shell at /authors and applies the static canonical SEO metadata.
uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: The canonical localized app shell renders the searchable directory, uses the public aggregate API and links to existing public author profiles.
uiLifecycle.servedBundleParity: public/app.js and public/app-17.23.0.js must remain byte-identical; authors-page.js loads before the versioned application bundle.

privacySecurity.authentication: The directory and aggregate endpoint are public and do not require a session.
privacySecurity.authorization: The endpoint exposes only author display names and aggregate counts derived from published, rights-eligible novels.
privacySecurity.ownerScoping: No account IDs, emails, private profile fields or unpublished works are returned.
privacySecurity.csrf: GET-only read surface; no state mutation.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: Raw trimmed search query above 80 characters returns HTTP 400 before database query preparation. Accepted search uses escaped LIKE literals and result rows are capped at 50 for search and 100 for directory.
privacySecurity.rightsAndPrivacy: Only original, public-domain, licensed or authorized published novels contribute to the public directory.

changeSummary: Reconstructs the missing public author directory as a bounded, localized feature slice on the canonical integration root. Reuses the existing public-author API but hardens search and aggregates, adds /authors routing and SEO/sitemap coverage, integrates desktop/mobile navigation, and synchronizes the editable and served app bundles. Adds a local Worker/D1 integration test and makes the 80-character search boundary explicit: overlong public-author queries receive HTTP 400 before SQL preparation.
acceptanceCriteria: /authors resolves to a dedicated authors.html shell and appears in the canonical route registry and static sitemap.
Desktop and mobile navigation expose the directory in all fourteen supported locales.
The client renders author names as text and links safely to existing /author/:name profiles.
The API is GET-only, caps q at 80 characters, escapes LIKE wildcard characters, and limits output to 50/100 rows.
Only published novels with original, public_domain, licensed or authorized rights contribute to aggregates.
Views are coalesced to zero and invalid ratings outside 1–10 are excluded from aggregates.
No private creator or account fields are returned.
SEO metadata is indexable and canonical; app.js and app-17.23.0.js are byte-identical.
Route, API method, authorization and sitemap inventories match the implemented behavior.
All six exact-head integration workflows pass; no production deployment or D1 migration is performed.
The public-author Worker rejects raw trimmed search input longer than 80 characters with HTTP 400 before preparing SQL; exact-head local D1 integration proves this boundary.
